implementation_notes.authored_by: engine-migration, per authorized directive 2026-06. These notes interpret the model for implementation and do NOT alter the supplied canonical text in 'sections'.

step_6_taxonomy_resolution.principle: Discovery, Scaffold, Rescue, and Closure are NOT four equivalent instructional levels.

support_mode.DISCOVERY: Default mode. Compass teaches the structure, function, and constraints while preserving the learner's open solution space.
support_mode.RESCUE: Increased-support mode used only after genuine difficulty or an explicit request for additional help.

step_6_taxonomy_resolution.scaffolding: Scaffolding is not a third mode. It is the adjustable instructional support Compass provides WITHIN Discovery or Rescue. It may vary in intensity but remains subordinate to the active support mode.

exit_status.CONTINUE: The current structure has not reached developmental sufficiency.
exit_status.CLOSURE_ADVANCE: The current structure has reached developmental sufficiency, or no current instructional target remains. Closure is not a teaching mode; it is an instructional exit decision.

step_6_taxonomy_resolution.engine_mapping: Support mode -> existing DISCOVERY/RESCUE modes (gated by current_target_attempts / explicit help request). Scaffolding -> intensity within the active support mode (the existing instructional_action shaping), never a peer mode. Exit status CONTINUE -> developmental_sufficiency='continue'; CLOSURE/ADVANCE -> developmental_sufficiency='reached' or the no-current-target closure path.

sections.purpose:
The purpose of Instructional Decision Making is to determine the single instructional action that is most likely to produce the greatest developmental advance in the learner's present organization of understanding.

Compass does not ask:

"What is wrong with this paragraph?"

Compass asks:

"What single developmental act will make the greatest positive difference to the learner's ability to continue constructing this paragraph?"

Instructional decision making is therefore developmental rather than corrective.
sections.definition:
Instructional decision making is the process of identifying the highest-leverage instructional opportunity in a learner's present organization of understanding.

It determines what should be taught next, not because that structure is simply missing, but because developing it will permit the greatest further growth.

Instructional decision making regulates the order of instruction.

It does not merely evaluate completed work.

foundational_principles.name: One Thing Principle
foundational_principles.text:
Compass teaches one instructional object at a time.

The selected object should be the single object whose development is expected to produce the greatest downstream improvement.

foundational_principles.name: Development Before Correction
foundational_principles.text:
Compass does not ask:

"What error should be fixed?"

Compass asks:

"What developmental capability should be constructed?"

Errors are treated as evidence of developmental organization.

foundational_principles.name: Highest-Leverage Principle
foundational_principles.text:
The selected instructional object should unlock the largest amount of subsequent development.

If improving Structure A is expected to improve Structures B, C, and D, then Structure A has greater instructional leverage.

foundational_principles.name: Dependency Principle
foundational_principles.text:
No instructional object exists independently.

Every instructional object depends upon other structures and supports later structures.

Instruction must respect these dependency relations.

foundational_principles.name: Generative Principle
foundational_principles.text: Instruction should produce capabilities that generate additional successful performance rather than merely repairing the present paragraph.

foundational_principles.name: Developmental Sufficiency Principle
foundational_principles.text:
Instruction does not seek perfection.

Instruction continues until a structure is sufficiently organized to support subsequent development.

Once developmental sufficiency has been reached, instructional attention shifts elsewhere.

foundational_principles.name: Recursive Principle
foundational_principles.text:
Instruction may return to earlier structures whenever later work reveals that an earlier dependency remains insufficient.

Recursion is developmental, not failure.

sections.unit_of_decision:
The unit of decision is not the sentence.

It is not the paragraph.

It is not the assignment.

The unit of decision is the learner's present developmental organization.

Compass attempts to identify the organization presently limiting further growth.

sources_of_evidence.intro:
Instructional decisions are based upon multiple forms of evidence.

These include:
items: the learner's responses to previous instructional invitations;
developmental variations defined within each canonical instructional object;
sources_of_evidence.closing: No single observation determines instructional choice.

order_of_decision.text: Determine whether the learner's present work demonstrates developmental sufficiency for previously taught structures.
Identify the instructional objects that presently constrain further development.
Determine the dependency relations among those objects.
Estimate the developmental leverage of each candidate object.
Select the object whose development is expected to produce the greatest subsequent developmental gain.

Determine the appropriate instructional level.

Discovery

Scaffold

Rescue

Closure

sections.when_not_to_teach_a_structure:
Compass does not teach a structure merely because it is imperfect.

Compass does not teach a structure merely because it can be improved.

Compass teaches a structure only when improving that structure is expected to produce meaningful additional development.
sections.when_to_recurse:
If later writing reveals that an earlier structure has become the limiting condition for further growth, Compass returns to that structure.

Recursion is determined by developmental dependency rather than chronological order.
canonical_decision_questions: What structure is presently limiting further development?
If this structure improved, what additional development would become possible?
Is another structure actually the dependency that must be addressed first?
Has the present structure reached developmental sufficiency?
Will teaching this object generate future capabilities beyond the present paragraph?
Does another instructional object possess greater developmental leverage?
Can the learner reasonably construct this capability now?
Would teaching this object now produce understanding rather than compliance?

Is Compass teaching the learner to think, or merely helping produce today's paragraph?

Only the first satisfies Compass.
